text: Hangzhou Lizhizao Precision Machinery Co., Ltd. The people behind your custom parts Custom CNC machining in Hangzhou, China. Prototypes and small production batches from drawings or samples, with orders starting at 1 piece. Meet LZZ Inside our factory Workshop visit and part discussion · January 2025 company archive. Founded in Hangzhou 2017 Production facility 1,500 m² CNC machines 40+ Prototypes and small batches From 1 piece Inside the LZZ machining workshop in Hangzhou. LZZ Precision Custom CNC machining at LZZ LZZ is an ISO 9001-certified CNC machining company. Our workshop combines milling, turning and multi-axis machining with dimensional inspection. How we work Inside our factory Company documents and certificate details How our capabilities developed 01 Founded in 2017 LZZ began making precision CNC machined parts for domestic equipment manufacturers. 02 More machining options We added CNC milling and turning equipment, along with multi-axis machines, to take on a wider range of industrial parts. 03 Production checks First-article checks became part of the workflow, alongside inspection during production and before shipment. 04 More inspection equipment CMM, height gauges and optical projectors allowed us to inspect more complex custom components. 05 Overseas customers We expanded our OEM/ODM machining services to customers in Asia, North America and Europe. Applications and example parts We manufacture custom parts for a range of industries. Send your drawing, intended use and applicable standards so we can review the requirements for your project. text: Capabilities / 5-axis machining 5-axis machining for complex geometry Machining for angled features and curved surfaces. We assess the geometry and tool access from your model. Prepare RFQ email ↗ Multi-bore circular milled component Scope Part examples Machining studies Drawing & inspection Enquiry Angled access and continuous contours Angled features may be reached by indexed positioning; continuous contours may need a simultaneous tool path. We review the model before choosing the machining route. Geometry & process For continuous curves, deep cavities and features requiring angled tool access. Impellers, curved components and multi-sided housings use angled tool access and contour machining. Size & workholding Review the clamping areas, tool reach and clearance across the required orientations. Identify protected surfaces and features that must share a setup; use the size-review checklist below to provide the model and dimensions. Material & finish Services cover aluminum, titanium, Inconel and hardened stainless. Specify the grade, material condition and finish requirements, including surfaces where tool marks matter. Review your part size & setup Include finished length, width, height and weight, stock dimensions and weight, protected surfaces, clamping areas and clearances. Send the model, drawing, material and quantity; machine travel, load and maximum part envelope are not published here. Request a size review ↗ Part examples Browse all parts ↗ Multi-bore circular milled component ↗ Machined impellers ↗ Ring housings & angled components ↗ Machining in practice All machining studies ↗ Five-axis machining for multi-face components Machining holes, side openings and contoured faces on a component held in a rotary setup. View process study ↗ Two milling setups for one part ↗ Two milling setups provide access to different faces of the same part. Choose the motion that the geometry needs 01 Indexed positioning Indexed 3+2 positioning presents an angled face to the tool, then cuts with the rotary axes held in position. 02 Simultaneous machining Simultaneous five-axis motion changes tool orientation during the cut for suitable continuous contours. We review the model to select the route. 03 Plan the complete route Workholding, stock size, tool reach and inspection access are reviewed together. The quote records the agreed process and deliverables. AI-generated geometry illustration. Not an LZZ part or inspection record. Drawing requirements Identify the functional surfaces and the relationships between angled holes, bores and mounting faces. Specify which model revision defines the contour. Mark restricted tool access, thin blades, deep cavities and surfaces where tool marks matter. Discuss acceptable changes before fixing the route. Specify pocket depth, corner radii and wall thickness; identify the datum face, hole pattern and thread specification. Define the side bore and its relationship to the other features. Inspection and acceptance Define profile and position requirements with usable datums. Agree the features to compare with the model or measure. For rotating or fluid-handling parts, identify any separate balance, leak or functional test requirement; geometry alone does not demonstrate performance. Agree the measurement method and required records before production. h1: Aluminum parts, made to your drawing
text: Capabilities / Aluminum machining Aluminum parts, made to your drawing Custom aluminum housings and structural components. Specify the alloy and finish needed for your application. Prepare RFQ email ↗ Aluminum intercooler prototypes Scope Part examples Machining studies Drawing & inspection Enquiry Aluminum housings and automotive prototypes For an enclosure, billet intake component or cooling prototype, review the thin sections and mounting interfaces together with the alloy, temper and finish. Geometry & process For lightweight housings, automotive prototypes and multi-feature components, including thin walls and deep pockets. Size & workholding Send a 3D model with the overall dimensions and stock size. Enclosure machining considers stress relief, fixture support and the order in which material is removed. Review tool access, clamping space and final interfaces together. Material & finish 6061/6061-T6 and 7075 appear across billet machining services; 3003 is also offered in the intercooler service. Select the grade and temper for the actual part. Bead blasting, brushing, polishing, anodizing, chemical conversion and powder coating are offered across relevant services. Define color and masking requirements. Grades to discuss Aluminum alloys: 6061 · 6061-T6 · 6063 · 6063-T5 · 7075 · 7075-T6 · 2024 · 5083 Specify the alloy and temper on the drawing. Availability and suitability for the part and finish are confirmed in the quotation. Part examples Browse all parts ↗ Aluminum intercooler prototypes ↗ Billet aluminum engine covers ↗ Billet intake manifold prototypes ↗ Machining in practice All machining studies ↗ Milling a pocketed enclosure-style component Milling a recessed component with a circular pocket and mounting features. View process study ↗ CNC machining a 29-inch display housing ↗ A broad display housing with recessed faces, edge details and mounting features. Custom metal parts in batches: shafts, fittings and housings ↗ Turned shafts, fittings and recessed housings: a selection of custom metal components in batches. More photographs from the workshop Machined display housing panel A complete panel with visible contours and slots; the source folder identifies a 29-inch display enclosure. Machined aluminum housings A group of housings showing pockets, bores and fastening features. Plan the alloy and finish together 01 Review We machine aluminum housings, brackets and prototype components to the specified alloy and temper. 02 Machine For thin walls and deep pockets, review support, stock removal and final interfaces before choosing the setup. 03 Finish & inspect Polishing, brushing, bead blasting and anodizing can be included in the order. Define cosmetic faces, masking and post-finish dimensions. Drawing requirements Specify alloy, temper and stock form. For housings, identify wall thicknesses, mounting datums, sealing faces and deep-pocket access. For anodized or other finished parts, mark masked fits, cosmetic faces and post-finish acceptance dimensions. Treat color requirements separately from geometry. Inspection and acceptance Agree checks for flatness, bore relationships and interfaces that control fit. Define surface acceptance using the intended finish. Specify pressure, leak or assembly tests separately. An automotive prototype in the catalog is not proof of tested vehicle performance. Agree the measurement method and required records before production. text: Capabilities / Casting machining Finished interfaces for cast components Machining cast housings, transmission components and pump bodies. Send the casting specification along with the finished-part drawing. Prepare RFQ email ↗ Transmission housings & pump bodies Scope Part examples Drawing & inspection Enquiry Finish machining for cast blanks The casting and finished-part drawings must show what remains as cast and where material is removed. Confirm blank supply and acceptance before planning the machining work. Geometry & process For adding finished bores, mounting faces, threads and passages to cast blanks. Milling, boring, drilling and tapping address transmission housings, pump bodies and structural enclosures. Reverse engineering support includes sample scanning, 2D/3D model reconstruction and manufacturability review. Size & workholding Share the blank model or photos, overall dimensions and casting and finished-part drawings. Fixtures for irregular blanks use casting datums, stock allowance and accessible clamping positions. Identify who supplies and approves the casting. h1: Engineering plastics, machined for your part
text: Capabilities / Plastic machining Engineering plastics, machined for your part Milled and turned engineering plastics for insulating parts and structural blocks. Browse examples by shape and function. Prepare RFQ email ↗ Non-metallic & insulating components Scope Part examples Machining studies Drawing & inspection Enquiry Plastic insulators, wear parts and housings Insulating plates, wear components and machined blocks place different demands on a polymer. Specify the grade for the operating environment and loads, then review the machining and measurement conditions. Geometry & process For insulating components, wear parts, seals and lightweight structural pieces. Milling and turning cover drilled blocks, gears, rollers, thin walls, deep pockets and multi-axis holes. Size & workholding Send a 3D model with the overall dimensions and stock size. Low-stress workholding and temperature control address deformation. Review clamping space, tool access, thin sections and assembly loads together. Material & finish PEEK, PTFE, polyimide, nylon, acetal/Delrin, HDPE, UHMW, acrylic and polycarbonate are listed in the plastic machining service. Specify the exact polymer grade, fillers and stock condition. Define edge quality, cleaning and mating-surface requirements. Grades to discuss Engineering plastics: POM (acetal) · PTFE · PEEK · Nylon · PA6 · PA66 · ABS · PC · PVC · PP Specify the polymer grade and condition. Acetal and Delrin are not treated as different base polymers here; confirm a branded grade if required. Specify the exact grade and any fillers. 02 Machine Review clamping, thin sections, temperature, moisture and assembly conditions before agreeing the machining and measurement approach. 03 Finish & inspect Deliverables can include dimensional results and material traceability. Electrical, medical or other application approval is a separate requirement, not a consequence of the material name. Drawing requirements Give the exact polymer grade, fillers and stock condition. Identify temperature, moisture, chemical exposure and electrical requirements relevant to selection. Mark thin walls and deep pockets, along with press fits and inserts. Include assembly loads and any permitted geometry changes. Inspection and acceptance Agree measurement and conditioning requirements where material behavior affects acceptance. Define hole position, flatness and mating-surface criteria. Specify edge, cleanliness and surface requirements; a product photograph is not evidence of electrical, food-contact or medical compliance. Agree the measurement method and required records before production. h1: Machined prototypes for your next revision
text: Capabilities / Prototype machining Machined prototypes for your next revision Machined prototypes for design development. Browse examples and discuss the next revision of your part. Prepare RFQ email ↗ Ring housings & angled components Scope Part examples Drawing & inspection Enquiry What should your prototype verify? Prototype examples focus on automotive housings and intake or cooling components. State the goal: packaging, assembly, appearance or a specific functional test. A prototype does not automatically validate a production design. Geometry & process For checking fit, assembly and design details before repeat production. STEP or IGES review helps identify tool access, fitment and manufacturability issues before machining. Automotive development examples include intercoolers, billet engine covers, intake manifolds, plenums and electronic throttle bodies. Size & workholding Send the current model revision, overall dimensions and stock size. Separate fixed interfaces from geometry still open to change so tool access and clamping space can be reviewed for the prototype. Material & finish Specify the material grade, condition and required finish. State whether production material and finish are essential to the evaluation, or whether alternatives may be proposed for your approval. Separate fit-check dimensions from appearance finishes. Drawing requirements Identify the current revision and dimensions needed for the prototype evaluation. Separate fixed interfaces from geometry still open to change. State whether production material and finish are essential to the evaluation, or whether alternatives may be proposed for your approval. Inspection and acceptance Agree the measurements and evidence needed to judge the prototype against its objective. Document the acceptance criteria for each critical interface. If testing is required, identify who supplies the fixture and test procedure and who evaluates the result. No test completion is implied by the example. Agree the measurement method and required records before production. h1: Stainless steel parts for your assembly
text: Capabilities / Stainless steel machining Stainless steel parts for your assembly Stainless steel shafts, fittings and other custom components machined to your drawing. Prepare RFQ email ↗ Stainless steel turned shafts Scope Part examples Drawing & inspection Enquiry Stainless steel shafts, fittings and hardware Choose the grade and condition for the operating environment, then specify the treatment and final dimensions. The listed grades are not interchangeable; photographs do not verify the material of a pictured part. Geometry & process For corrosion-resistant shafts, fittings, valve parts and locking components. Shafts, flanges, grooves and threads can be combined with live-tool flats, cross-holes and engraving. Size & workholding Send a 3D model with the overall dimensions and stock size. Identify working diameters, shoulders and off-axis features so tool access, clamping space and the assembly datums can be reviewed. Material & finish 303, 304, 316L and 17-4PH options serve different machining and operating requirements. Specify the grade and material condition, including any required heat treatment. Fine turning, polishing, passivation and electropolishing are offered across the stainless services. Specify the treatment and required final dimensions. Grades to discuss Stainless steel: SUS303 · SUS304 · SUS316 · SUS316L · SUS430 · SUS440 Specify the exact grade and condition. Corrosion, strength, finishing and documentation needs must be reviewed for the intended use. Part examples Browse all parts ↗ Stainless steel turned shafts ↗ Stainless steel turned parts ↗ Indexing plungers & locking pins ↗ Specify the working surfaces, not just the grade 01 Review We machine stainless shafts, fittings and housings with turned and milled features. State the alloy and material condition on the drawing. 02 Machine Review mating diameters, threads, burr-sensitive edges and the service environment together. 03 Finish & inspect Polishing, passivation and electropolishing are service options; the required finish and dimensional acceptance belong in the order specification. Drawing requirements Specify the grade and material condition, including any required heat treatment. Identify working diameters, threads and sealing or sliding surfaces. State the service environment and selected surface treatment; corrosion resistance and compatibility must be evaluated for the actual application. Inspection and acceptance Define runout, diameter and thread checks in relation to the assembly datums. Mark surfaces where burrs or handling marks are unacceptable. Request any material or treatment documents you need. Confirm their availability and contents before placing an order. Agree the measurement method and required records before production. If passivation or electropolishing is requested, specify the applicable requirements and the dimensions that must be accepted after treatment. text: Privacy & site information Information about inquiry drafts, browser storage and the product details on this site. Your inquiry The form creates an email draft in your browser. It does not send your information to LZZ or upload drawings. To contact us, open the draft in your email app, add your attachments and send it yourself. Saved drafts The form saves your input and draft status in the current tab using sessionStorage, with a separate entry for each selected part. Your details stay available after a refresh but are not saved to an account or sent to LZZ. Select "Clear saved input" to remove the entry for the current part. Your browser may restore this data when it restores a previous session. Clear your input before leaving a shared device. If browser storage is blocked or full, you can still use the form while the page is open. Select "Save draft" to download a text copy. Cookies and external services This site does not use analytics or advertising cookies. Your email provider, WhatsApp and other linked websites have their own privacy policies. Product and company information Product pages use catalog photographs and clearly labeled illustrative visuals. Neither is an inspection record or a specification document. Original workshop photographs and company documents are identified separately from product examples. Product pages use shorter titles and summaries of the catalog entries. Original catalog names and source material are retained in our archive; they are not displayed on every product page. The summaries are not independently verified specifications for the photographed parts. Confirm material grades and tolerances with the team, along with the inspection and commercial terms for your order. The engineering guides help you prepare an inquiry; they are not inspection records or customer case studies. They do not establish suitability for a particular application. Material filters help you find existing parts without creating duplicate product pages. English descriptions of company documents explain their contents but do not verify current validity. Contact For questions, contact roger@lzz-cnc.com .

h1: CNC milling vs turning vs 5-axis machining: how to choose
text: Resources Process comparison CNC milling vs turning vs 5-axis machining: how to choose On this page Compare the processes by geometry When does a part need more than one process? Is 5-axis machining always more accurate? What should I include when asking for a process recommendation? A shaft or sleeve will usually start with turning. A housing with pockets and flat mounting faces is more likely to need milling. Angled features or access to several faces may call for a multi-axis setup. Some parts need a combination; send the drawing so we can review the sequence. CNC turning operation; original LZZ process photograph. CNC milling operation photographed in LZZ process materials; source folder dated December 2025. Five-axis machining operation; original LZZ process photograph. Compare the processes by geometry Route to discuss Geometry cues Drawing and quote questions CNC turning Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis. Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling. CNC milling Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces. Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records. Multi-axis machining Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches. Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model. CNC turning Geometry cues Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis. Drawing and quote questions Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling. CNC milling Geometry cues Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces. Drawing and quote questions Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records. Multi-axis machining Geometry cues Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches. Drawing and quote questions Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model. When does a part need more than one process? A shaft with cross-holes, a turned fitting with milled flats or a housing with angled faces may need more than one operation or setup. The route should preserve the relationships between critical features. Send a 3D model and controlled 2D drawing so the team can review datums, access and inspection together. Is 5-axis machining always more accurate? No single process label guarantees accuracy. Acceptance depends on the part geometry, machine and setup, datum strategy, material, finishing and measurement method. If an interface matters, state its tolerance and datum on the drawing and ask how it will be produced and checked. Any tolerance target needs feature-specific review. What should I include when asking for a process recommendation? A 3D model and the controlling 2D drawing revision. Material grade and condition, or the functional requirement if still undecided. Quantity for the first order and expected repeat pattern, if known. Critical datums, fits, surface requirements and required inspection records. Finish, packaging and required arrival date, with any standards or approvals identified. Use the RFQ checklist to organize those details. We review your drawing before confirming the machining process and quoting a price and schedule. Apply the guide Related part examples Compare the features in these examples with your drawing. text: Resources Manufacturing guide Planning CNC parts for prototypes and repeat orders On this page Identify the working surfaces Specify critical dimensions Specify material and finish Agree on prototype checks Confirm repeat-order requirements Identify the working surfaces For a housing or shaft, the surfaces that meet other parts matter as much as the outside shape. The same applies to a mounting block. Mark the surfaces that locate, seal, slide or carry load on the drawing so you can discuss tolerances in relation to their function. Compare milled pockets and housings with turned shafts and fittings . Some designs need both operations; the geometry determines the process choice. Specify critical dimensions Give the datums and mating details for critical features, with their acceptance limits. A 3D model shows the shape but may leave fits or surface texture undefined. It may also omit edge conditions and measurement methods. Include a controlled 2D drawing when these requirements apply. Tolerances need review against the specific drawing. The material and feature geometry affect the assessment, as do the setup and measurement method; a single tolerance cannot apply to every catalog part. Agree on inspection requirements and supporting records for your design. Specify material and finish State the exact alloy or plastic grade and any material-certificate requirement. For coated parts, specify the finish and whether critical dimensions apply before or after treatment. Mark areas that need masking, cosmetic faces and burr-sensitive edges. The material and finish checklist covers these details. Catalog photographs show shapes and surfaces; they cannot establish a coating specification or provide material certification. Agree on prototype checks Explain the purpose of the prototype. You may need to check assembly fit and access, assess appearance or run a functional test. Agree on the checks needed for revision or approval. If the design changes, issue a revised drawing with the affected dimensions identified; an email description alone is not enough. The prototype machining examples show trial parts. When requesting a quote, separate the trial quantity from expected repeat orders. Orders start at 1 piece. Production takes 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing; transit is additional. Confirm price and inspection requirements for your project. Confirm repeat-order requirements Use the approved drawing revision and confirm the material and finish. Agree on the inspection scope and packaging requirements before ordering. If you need a first-article report or material documents, confirm their format and availability. Sample approval does not cover a changed design or material. For orders like the low-volume parts shown here, use the RFQ checklist to prepare your inquiry. text: Resources Delivery planning Shipping CNC parts internationally Include the destination and required arrival date in your RFQ. Packing, documents and transport responsibilities need to be agreed alongside the machining work. A quotation checklist See the shipping checklist On this page Part protection Pack identification Delivery basis Documents Schedule Shipping checklist Five topics to confirm before a quotation Use this checklist to distinguish the information you provide from the details to confirm in the quotation. Topic Information you provide Confirm in the quotation 01 Part protection Information you provide Cosmetic faces, sealing surfaces, threads, fragile edges, cleanliness and corrosion-protection needs. Confirm in the quotation Protective materials, separation between parts, carton or case requirements and packing limits. 02 Pack identification Information you provide Part number, drawing revision, quantity per pack, batch identification and required labels. Confirm in the quotation Whether labels, lot references and inspection documents are available in your requested format. 03 Delivery basis Information you provide Full delivery address, receiving contact, required arrival date, requested trade term/version and named place. Confirm in the quotation Who books transport and handles export/import clearance, insurance, duties, taxes and local delivery. 04 Documents Information you provide The document list required by procurement, logistics or your destination-side import contact. Confirm in the quotation Which documents are available for this order and who prepares each. Requirements depend on the destination and transaction. 05 Schedule Information you provide Separate your required arrival date from the desired dispatch date. Confirm in the quotation Production takes 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Estimate transit separately. From the packing archive LZZ packing archive LZZ packing archive · November 2022. Packing varies by part, quantity and route. These images do not establish a customer, destination, carrier, trade term or delivery outcome for a new order. AI-generated packing illustration · Not an LZZ shipment. Packing for international delivery Protect finished surfaces and threads Packing depends on the part and transport route. Mark vulnerable surfaces and describe any receiving limits so protection can be specified in the quotation. Separate and protect Agree protective materials to separate parts and protect threads and mating surfaces. Mark critical surfaces Identify cosmetic faces, sealing surfaces, fragile edges and areas requiring cleanliness or corrosion protection. Pack for the route Confirm cartons or wooden cases according to the part, quantity and transport method. Consider receiving limits Specify pack weight or quantity limits and any handling requirements at the receiving site. Keep identification and documents together AI-generated identification illustration · Not an order record. Part identification links to the packing list Provide the part number, drawing revision, quantity per pack and batch identification. Agree the label, lot-reference and inspection-document formats available for your order. Use the same part and revision references on the packing list and agreed quality records. Agree destination-specific documents We provide protective packing, a packing list, commercial invoice and shipment information. Material, finishing and dimensional records are included when specified in the order. Agree additional customs documents before production with your importing entity or freight forwarder. Agree the delivery basis Destination, transport and responsibilities Confirm the destination, delivery requirements and responsibilities in your quotation. EXW, FOB or DDP options are quoted for the applicable destination and service; DDP is not an automatic inclusion. Transport method Courier, air or sea arrangements depend on shipment size and destination. DHL, FedEx or UPS can be discussed when selecting a courier. Trade term and named place State the requested term, version and named place. Confirm who arranges transport, export/import clearance, insurance, duties, taxes and local delivery. Production and transit time Production takes 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Transit is estimated separately and is not included in production time. Related part examples Each custom part requires its own drawing and quote. Complex aluminum housings Learn more How We Work RFQ Checklist Back to Resources Include delivery in your RFQ Send the controlled drawing, material and finish specification, quantity, delivery address, packing requirements, requested arrival date and document list. Ask the quote to identify the trade term and named place, production schedule basis, transit assumption, carrier responsibility and any exclusions. Prepare RFQ email Review your draft before sending it from your email app. roger@lzz-cnc.com

text: Resources Frequently asked questions Custom CNC machining FAQ What to send for a quote, how production time is counted, and which inspection and shipping details to agree before ordering. FAQ topics Quotes & ordering Preparing a quotation Processes & specifications Inspection & delivery Case studies & further resources Minimum order From 1 piece Share first-order and expected repeat quantities for separate quotes. Production 7–14 business days After drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional. To quote Drawing + specifications Send drawing revision, units, material, finish, quantity and destination. Quotes & ordering What is the minimum order quantity? Orders start at 1 piece. Include your first-order quantity and expected repeat quantities so the quotation can distinguish prototype work from future batches. What is the production lead time? Production takes 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional. Record the confirmed production schedule and delivery arrangements in your quotation and order. Preparing a quotation What should I send for a quotation? Please provide the following information: Drawing revision and units Exact material grade and condition Finish and surface treatment First-order and expected repeat quantities Delivery destination STEP model, where available Dimensioned 2D drawing with critical tolerances, threads and acceptance requirements Does the website send my inquiry or upload my drawing? No. The inquiry form prepares an email draft. Check the draft, open it in your email application, attach your drawings and send it there. Copy and download options are also available; preparing a draft does not send an inquiry to LZZ. Processes & specifications Which machining services can I discuss with LZZ? Our five service areas are CNC milling, CNC turning, five-axis CNC machining, plastic machining and casting machining. Share the complete part geometry so the route, workholding and finishing requirements can be reviewed together. For castings, agree who supplies and approves the blank. How should I specify the material and finish? Specify the exact material grade and condition, not just aluminum, steel or plastic. Identify cosmetic faces, surface treatment requirements, masking and dimensions that must be checked after finishing. The quotation should record the agreed specification. Can every feature hold ±0.01 mm? No. ±0.01 mm is a conditional engineering reference for selected critical features after review, not a general part tolerance or guarantee. Material, geometry, setup and measurement method determine whether it applies. Identify each critical feature on the drawing for confirmation. Inspection & delivery Which inspection documents should I request? Specify the required dimensional results, first-article records, material traceability and finishing documents before ordering. Agree the features, sampling and report format. The quotation records the included document package and any additional cost; request current calibration evidence separately where needed. Is LZZ ISO 9001 certified? LZZ is ISO 9001 certified. For supplier qualification, request the current certificate for Hangzhou Lizhizao Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., including its number, issuer, validity, scope and verification details. Company awards are separate from the ISO certificate, and quality-system certification does not replace part-specific acceptance or industry approval. How are packing and international shipping agreed? Provide the destination, receiving requirements and any vulnerable or cosmetic surfaces that need protection. Confirm the packing method, transport method, trade term and named place in the quotation. Agree the packing list, commercial invoice and other required documents. Transit time is separate from production time. Case studies & further resources What do the machining case studies demonstrate? The studies use original LZZ workshop photographs to discuss visible part features, machining sequences and drawing questions. They are not customer performance reports, inspection results or proof of a particular delivery outcome. h1: Specifying material and finish for a machined part
text: Resources Design preparation Specifying material and finish for a machined part On this page Finishing services and acceptance points Describe the operating conditions Specify the material grade Material examples named in the original brochure Compare material families by the job How should I compare material options? Define the finish requirements Resolve dimensions after treatment Record the requirements in your RFQ Finishing services and acceptance points We support deburring, bead blasting, polishing, anodizing, passivation and plating as appropriate to the selected material. The quotation defines the finish and any accompanying documents; not every treatment is suitable for every alloy. Deburring and polishing: specify edge breaks, cosmetic faces and any controlled roughness. Bead blasting: agree appearance, protected interfaces and whether a reference sample is needed. Anodizing: specify alloy, color, coating requirements and masked threads or mating surfaces. Passivation and plating: identify the applicable material, process specification, protected areas and acceptance documents. Critical dimensions are checked at the agreed stage, including after finishing where required. We link the material and treatment documents requested in the order to the relevant part or batch reference. AI-generated illustrative image. It does not identify alloy grades, stock availability or finish specifications. Describe the operating conditions Explain the weight and loading requirements, along with the part's exposure and operating temperature. Describe its electrical behavior and the assembly it mates with. If you have not selected a grade, share these conditions and the applicable specification for engineering review. A catalog category does not establish suitability for a safety-critical application. Specify the material grade The catalog groups parts by material: aluminum , stainless steel , copper and brass , and engineering plastics . Each group covers different grades. State the grade and condition your design requires, then confirm whether alternatives are permitted and which material documents you need. Material examples named in the original brochure Aluminum: 6061, 7075 and 2024. Stainless steel: 304, 316 and 17-4PH. Copper and brass: printed as C3600 and H62 in the source brochure. Engineering plastics: POM, PEEK and PPSU. Other named materials: titanium, Inconel, Kovar and Invar. This list preserves examples from the source brochure; it does not confirm current stock or availability. Confirm the exact alloy designation, grade, condition, process suitability and material documents for each part. In particular, verify the intended C3600 designation before quoting. Compare material families by the job Family Examples in the brochure Compare and confirm Aluminum 6061, 7075, 2024 Compare strength/stiffness, part mass, environment and finish needs. Confirm exact alloy/temper, alternatives, finish compatibility and documents. Stainless steel 304, 316, 17-4PH Compare environment, mechanical requirements and condition. Confirm grade, heat treatment where applicable, finish, standard and certificates. Copper / brass C3600, H62 as printed Compare electrical or thermal role and service environment. Confirm the alloy designation and material documents. Check the brochure's C3600 reference with us before ordering. Engineering plastics POM, PEEK, PPSU Compare temperature, load, chemical exposure, electrical behavior and mating material. Confirm exact grade, operating conditions and traceability documents. Aluminum Examples in the brochure 6061, 7075, 2024 Compare and confirm Compare strength/stiffness, part mass, environment and finish needs. Confirm exact alloy/temper, alternatives, finish compatibility and documents. Stainless steel Examples in the brochure 304, 316, 17-4PH Compare and confirm Compare environment, mechanical requirements and condition. Confirm grade, heat treatment where applicable, finish, standard and certificates. Copper / brass Examples in the brochure C3600, H62 as printed Compare and confirm Compare electrical or thermal role and service environment. Confirm the alloy designation and material documents. Check the brochure's C3600 reference with us before ordering. Engineering plastics Examples in the brochure POM, PEEK, PPSU Compare and confirm Compare temperature, load, chemical exposure, electrical behavior and mating material. Confirm exact grade, operating conditions and traceability documents. These are comparison prompts, not a material recommendation. Properties vary by grade, condition and design; confirm the requirements with the drawing and applicable specification. How should I compare material options? A material family alone is not a purchase specification. Compare named grades using the conditions above, then record the grade, condition and applicable standard. If a substitute is proposed, approve it explicitly and confirm the available material documents. Define the finish requirements Specify visual appearance separately from the finish's function. Name the required finish standard and revision where applicable, and describe color, gloss, texture, coating thickness or roughness only where these are controlled requirements. Mark masked areas, cosmetic faces and surfaces for corrosion protection, electrical contact or sealing. Confirm process suitability, availability and required documentation for the selected material and part. A photograph shows surface appearance but cannot establish coating thickness or surface roughness. It cannot verify process compliance either, so a reference image alone is not a finish specification. AI-generated illustration. The pictured finishes are not LZZ samples and do not identify a coating, roughness value or process standard. Resolve dimensions after treatment Tell the supplier whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after finishing. Highlight mating bores, threads and other interfaces where a coating matters. Specify edge breaks and cosmetic faces separately so functional and appearance criteria can be reviewed together. Record the requirements in your RFQ Put the agreed material and finish requirements on the controlled drawing or specification. Include inspection and traceability needs in your RFQ package , using the quality checklist to check the details before you prepare an inquiry . Apply the guide Related part examples Compare the features in these examples with your drawing. Each part is quoted to its own specification. text: Resources Production planning CNC prototypes and small-batch production A prototype helps you check the design before ordering more parts. For a repeat batch, use the approved drawing revision and confirm the material and finish. You also need an agreed inspection plan and delivery terms. On this page Validate Approve Repeat Compare suppliers Next batch RFQ Validate. Check fit, function or appearance with a first sample. Approve. Lock the drawing, material and finish with agreed inspection. Repeat. Carry the approved specification into controlled production. AI-generated illustration — not an LZZ order or production record. 01 Validate the first sample Agree what the sample must prove: assembly fit, a critical interface, operation or appearance. Define the checks needed for sample acceptance before moving to a repeat order. Drawing questions Use the sample to identify design questions related to fit, function or appearance. Workholding and access Review workholding and tool access while confirming the design. Material, finish and acceptance Check the specified grade, condition and final appearance. Define fit, function and sample acceptance checks. Confirm the prototype price and schedule for the specific part. 02 Approve what will repeat For a repeat order, release one controlled drawing revision and carry the approved material and finish into the quotation. Agree the acceptance plan and the documents to accompany delivery. Specification to carry forward Agree revision approval and how changed features are identified. Confirm material documents and the finish standard, including masking and dimensions after treatment. Retain the approved specification unless a change is agreed. Evidence to agree Define batch sampling and critical-feature records. Confirm the measurement method, instrument evidence and available report format. Agree the acceptance plan and delivery documents. If the drawing changes, pause and confirm the impact. The old sample may no longer represent the new revision. 03 Plan the repeat order Confirm the setup and machining sequence for the released revision, including critical datums, and whether the route changes with quantity. Request a new quote for the batch quantity and price, and confirm the production slot. There is no fixed quantity threshold for an economical small batch. Economics depend on the part geometry and its setup. Minimum order 1 piece Production lead time 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional. Share the part, quantity and required arrival date so we can quote price and delivery arrangements. Compare suppliers before committing Compare the quoted scope, not headline unit price alone. Use the same drawing revision, material and finish, and check the following points with each supplier. Same specification Make sure each quote uses the same drawing revision, material and finish. What is included Check setup, inspection records, packaging and delivery basis are stated. Exclusions or substitutions Confirm that any exclusions or substitutions are clear. Changes and repeat orders Ask how changes, nonconforming parts and repeat orders will be handled. Related part examples The engine-cover example covers prototype clearances; the enclosure example covers thin walls and batch inspection. Billet aluminum engine covers Small-batch aluminum enclosures Back to Resources Ordering guide What to include in your next batch RFQ Share the drawing, first-order quantity, expected repeat pattern and required arrival date. Identify critical dimensions and records, then confirm price, production slot, inspection evidence, finish, packing and shipping terms for that order. The ordering guide explains the information to agree before shipment. Prepare RFQ email roger@lzz-cnc.com

text: Resources RFQ Checklist CNC machining RFQ checklist Prepare the drawing revision, material, quantity and acceptance requirements together. This checklist covers the technical files and order details we need to quote your part. On this page Five essential requirements Drawing and acceptance Material and final surface Drawing review Commercial brief Prepare the email Five essential requirements for a complete RFQ Drawing revision 3D model and 2D drawing when needed, part number, units and revision. Material & finish Exact material or functional requirement, finish details and applicable standards. Acceptance criteria Critical dimensions, datums, tolerances and inspection requirements. Quantity Initial quantity and expected repeat pattern. Delivery Arrival date, packaging, shipping basis and relevant customs requirements. Download order acceptance checklist A buyer worksheet to record drawing revision, critical features, documents and shipping requirements. AI-generated illustration — not an LZZ order or inspection record. Define how the part will be accepted Send a consistent drawing package Include a 3D model, such as STEP, and a 2D drawing when dimensions, fits or surface requirements are not fully defined in the model. Label the part number, units and drawing revision. If the files disagree, identify which document controls before requesting a quotation. For multi-axis parts, include the overall envelope, stock dimensions and part weight where known so tool access and setup can be reviewed. Only have a sample? For an existing sample without a drawing, explain what is known and ask what additional measurement or design work would be needed. A sample alone cannot establish hidden material or treatment requirements. Mark the dimensions used for acceptance Identify mating bores and shaft fits on the drawing, with their datums and tolerances. Mark sealing faces, threads and any other critical features too. State whether dimensions apply before or after finishing. If you need a particular inspection record, send the format or an example with your inquiry. Agree on inspection and documentation requirements before ordering, and ask LZZ to confirm the measurement method, instrument range, calibration evidence and availability of any project-specific records required for your part. Inspection & documentation requirements Specify the material and final surface Define the material, finish and applicable standards on your drawing or in your RFQ notes. Material requirements State the exact alloy or polymer grade, or the functional requirement if selection is still open. Include any required material documentation and whether substitutes may be considered. Finish and surface requirements Provide the finish specification, appearance, cosmetic faces, masking and edge conditions. Include any customer or industry standards and certificates required for this part or program. State the required standard, revision and scope. A material or capability category on this site does not establish industry certification or application compliance. The material and finish checklist explains the decisions behind these fields. What drawing review returns Our quotation brings together the proposed process, material, finishing, order quantity, inspection documents, production schedule and shipping basis. Where geometry or acceptance requirements need clarification, we identify the open points before you approve production. Use the order acceptance checklist to record the drawing revision, critical features, documents and shipping requirements in one place. This is a buyer worksheet, not an inspection report. Set the commercial brief Provide quantity, delivery and commercial details so we can confirm the scope and timing in your quotation. Minimum order 1 piece Production lead time 7–14 business days After drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Transit time is additional. Initial quantity Quantity per part number. Repeat pattern Expected repeat orders, if known. Delivery details Required arrival date and postcode. Packaging Any special packaging requirements. Shipping basis Incoterm and customs, duties or taxes responsibilities. Response deadline Your decision or response deadline, if applicable. Related part examples Fittings need defined threads and sealing faces; housings need mating datums and cavity details. These examples show the drawing questions for each. Turned fittings, connectors & flanges Complex aluminum housings Ready to prepare the email? If your project needs an NDA or a controlled transfer method, contact LZZ before sending restricted files. This website does not automatically create an NDA. Prepare the draft on the inquiry page. Attach drawings in your email application. Review the recipients and send when ready. The inquiry page prepares an email draft locally. The website does not upload drawings or send your request. Prepare RFQ email roger@lzz-cnc.com
